title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-nina-cho
body:
Context:
- Machine: gpu-infer-03 (prod-like dev box)
- GPU: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04
- Kernel: 5.15.0-80-generic
- Docker base: nvidia/cuda:11.7.1-cudnn8-runtime-ubuntu22.04 (used for container)
- Problem observed: intermittent CUDA OOMs during inference of Llama-2-13B-Chat quantized (4-bit) under continuous streaming load. Also saw driver/runtime mismatch error on one restart.

Repro steps (commands I ran):
1) Check GPU and driver on host
   - nvidia-smi -a
     -> shows NVIDIA-SMI 470.199.02 and Driver Version: 470.199.02, CUDA Version: 11.4

2) Check nvcc inside container (when container has CUDA toolkit)
   - docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:11.7.1-cudnn8-runtime-ubuntu22.04 nvcc --version
     -> shows nvcc: NVIDIA (R) Cuda compiler driver 11.7

3) Check torch and cuda availability inside container (python)
   - import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available())
     -> '2.2.0+cu117', '11.7', True

4) Reproduce minimal OOM with small script (in container)
   - python run_infer.py --model l2-13b-chat --batch 4 --seq 2048 --stream
   - Error: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.23 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 36.75 GiB already allocated)

5) Error seen on a restart (different run):
   - CUDA error: driver shutting down
   - stderr included: cudaGetDeviceCount: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version

6) Inspect container libraries:
   - ldd $(python -c "import torch; print(torch.__file__)" )/lib/libtorch.so | grep cuda || true
   - shows libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (compat from host driver)

Notes / initial hypotheses:
- Host driver reports 470.x (CUDA driver 11.4), container/toolkit/torch expect CUDA 11.7. Usually backward compatibility allows newer runtime to run on older driver up to a point, but 470 is fairly old relative to 11.7. The cudaGetDeviceCount message indicates a mismatch in one occurrence (driver too old for runtime).
- OOMs: model size, batch*seq combination seems to exceed available memory when KV cache grows (streaming). The reported 36.75 GiB allocated suggests some memory leak or fragmentation; expected baseline should be lower (~22-28 GiB) for 13B with quantization and 4-bit kernels.
- Possible culprits: mixed installations (pip wheel compiled for different CUDA), multiple processes pinning memory (torchserve/gunicorn), CUDA driver version mismatch causing incorrect cudaMalloc behavior, or reuse of GPU memory across runs due to driver not fully releasing resources on crash.

Commands/tricks tried and immediate results:
- Reduced batch size to 1 and seq to 1024 -> reduces OOM frequency but still occasionally OOMs under sustained requests.
- torch.cuda.empty_cache() before starting inference loop -> some transient improvement but doesn't fix leak.
- Used torch.backends.cudnn.enabled=False -> no change in OOM profile (but slower).
- model.eval(); for p in model.parameters(): p.requires_grad=False -> sanity check (no gradients).
- Restarted nvidia-persistenced and entire docker daemon -> temporary fix (cleared allocations), but on heavy load OOM returns.
- docker run --gpus all --rm my-image:latest nvidia-smi dmon -s u -> observed GPU memory spikes correlating with streaming long context windows.
- strace inside container showed a few calls to cuMemAlloc failing intermittently. Coupled with driver mismatch earlier, suggests driver/runtime inconsistency.

More detailed error snippets captured:
- "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.23 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 36.75 GiB already allocated)
  (CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call)"
- "cudaGetDeviceCount: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version"
- Kernel log when driver-shutdown happened: "NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus." (need to gather full dmesg next time)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Driver/runtime mismatch (medium-high): Host driver (470.x) too old for cu117-based runtime and torch 2.2. Intermittent "insufficient for runtime" messages support this. Risk: can produce undefined behavior and allocation failures.
2) Memory fragmentation or leak in inference code (medium): Streaming long contexts + persistent cache may fragment memory leading to eventual allocation failure. Might be exacerbated by custom kernels for 4-bit quantization (bitsandbytes or custom CUDA ops) leaking device memory.
3) Multiple processes / stray python processes holding memory (low-medium): Check ps aux | grep python across nodes; orphaned processes could steal memory.
4) Hardware error leading to driver reset (low): "GPU has fallen off the bus" points to potential hardware/PCIe issues. But less likely given most runs succeed and only heavy sustained runs fail.

Evidence to check next:
- Confirm host driver version across nodes (nvidia-smi) and upgrade matrix. For cu117/two2.2, recommended driver >= 515? Need to check compatibility table.
- Collect full dmesg and /var/log/syslog around time of driver shutdown to confirm "fell off the bus" events.
- Reproduce inside a container built with CUDA 11.4 base image (match host) and run the same torch wheel; compare behavior.
- Run a small alloc/free loop to test cudaMalloc/cudaFree stability over time (script that allocates random buffers frequently).
- Instrument code to log torch.cuda.memory_allocated() and memory_reserved() over time and on exception to see growth pattern.
- Check for bitsandbytes / custom extension versions: pip list | grep -E "bitsandbytes|xformers|triton" and ldd on their .so for libcuda linking.

Quick fixes attempted (temporary):
- Rebuild docker image to use nvidia/cuda:11.4.2-cudnn8-runtime-ubuntu22.04 to match driver 470 (short-term) -> Deploying to one test node next.
- Switched to torch wheel compiled for cu117 earlier; possibility to test a CPU-only or cpu offload approach to avoid immediate OOM for crashproofing.
- Added retry/cleanup loop in inference runner to call torch.cuda.empty_cache() and force gc.collect() between requests (band-aid).

Longer-term options:
- Standardize on host driver >= 515 (or per compatibility) across fleet and move to CUDA 11.7 images + torch cu117 wheels. This is preferable for performance and newer drivers.
- Add nightly stress tests that run streaming long-context workloads and watch for memory leaks.
- Add process-level watchdog to kill and restart inference process when memory usage grows beyond threshold.

Action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Gather dmesg and kernel logs for the PID/times when "GPU has fallen off the bus" occurred. (owner: Nina)
- [ ] Test with CUDA 11.4 base image (build variant) to see whether runtime-driver alignment fixes the issue. (owner: Nina)
- [ ] Run small cudaMalloc stress test for stability for 1 hour on gpu-infer-03. (owner: Raja)
- [ ] Confirm bitsandbytes version and whether it uses custom CUDA kernels that may leak memory; try latest release. (owner: Asha)
- [ ] Decide driver upgrade plan if tests point to driver mismatch (coord with infra). (owner: eng-platform)

Notes for follow-up:
- If driver upgrade is required, coordinate maintenance window; a driver upgrade will require node reboot and impacts running Dedicated capacity.
- If bitsandbytes is leaking memory, consider switching to alternate quant backend or use cpu offload for KV cache.
- Add logging around allocation sizes and keep a rolling 5-min histogram of allocation attempts to help diagnose fragmentation vs. steady leak.

Reference commands I'll paste into ticket / runbook:
- nvidia-smi -q -d MEM
- docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:11.4.2-cudnn8-runtime-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi -a
- python -c "import torch, time; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda);
  from torch import cuda;
  for i in range(10000):
    a = cuda.mem_alloc(1024*1024*20) if hasattr(cuda, 'mem_alloc') else torch.empty(1024*1024*5, device='cuda');
    if i % 100 == 0: print(i, torch.cuda.memory_allocated()); time.sleep(0.01)"

Last quick notes: keep both driver/runtime checks in CI for our inference images. We should add a small script that compares host nvidia-smi CUDA version to container torch.version.cuda on startup and warns (or blocks) if mismatch is outside supported range.

-- Nina
